title: Signed shift, associator and symmetry identities on total cochain tensors
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small relative to the universe of its ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal O$ commutative. Use integer-indexed cochain complexes, $E[a]^p=E^{p+a}$ and $d_{E[a]}=(-1)^a d_E$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the direct-sum total tensor $T(E,F)$ with differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For arbitrary, possibly unbounded complexes $E,F,G$ and integers $a,b,c$, the summand formulas
$$t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}:T(E[a],F[b])\xrightarrow{\sim}T(E,F)[a+b],\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto(-1)^{bp}x\otimes y\quad(x\in E[a]^p,\ y\in F[b]^q),$$
$$\alpha^{\rm Ch}:T(T(E,F),G)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(E,T(F,G)),\qquad (x\otimes y)\otimes z\longmapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z),$$
$$\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E,F}:T(E,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(F,E),\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x\quad(x\in E^p,\ y\in F^q)$$
define natural chain isomorphisms, uniquely specified by these summand formulas. In terms of the integer bifunctor shift comparisons $s^1,s^2$ of the additive bifunctor $\otimes_{\mathcal O}$ [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], $t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}=s^1_a(E,F)[b]\circ s^2_b(E[a],F)$, since $s^2_b$ multiplies the summand of first-factor degree $p$ by $(-1)^{bp}$ and $s^1_a$ is unsigned. The inverse of $t^{\rm Ch}$ has the same scalar on the reverse reindexing, the inverse associator is reverse reassociation, and the inverse symmetry is $\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{F,E}$.

With ordinary reassociation and the canonical equalities of shift indices understood, the following are identities of natural chain maps:
$$t^{\rm Ch}_{a+b,c}\circ T(t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b},1)=t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b+c}\circ T(1,t^{\rm Ch}_{b,c}),$$
as maps from the triple shifted tensor to $T(E,T(F,G))[a+b+c]$, with the appropriate $\alpha^{\rm Ch}$ on the source and the shifted target, and
$$\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E,F}[a+b]\circ t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}=(-1)^{ab}t^{\rm Ch}_{b,a}\circ\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E[a],F[b]}.$$
On shifted triple degree $(p,q,r)$ the two shift-extraction coefficients in the first identity are $(-1)^{bp+c(p+q)}$ and $(-1)^{cq+(b+c)p}$, respectively. On shifted bidegree $(p,q)$ the two coefficients in the second identity are $(-1)^{bp+(p+a)(q+b)}$ and $(-1)^{ab+pq+aq}$, respectively. These formulas hold for negative as well as positive integers. No flatness, localization, or degree-zero source is assumed.

proof.text: Work in the module universe in which the site is small. The module-sheaf category is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The reflector [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] exists here and is additive: a left adjoint preserves the zero object and finite coproducts, and addition is diagonal followed by the two maps and codiagonal in a biproduct. To check the local-equivalence hypothesis of the native-constraint node, first use [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]: set sheafification preserves finite products, as does the inclusion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-abelian-group-objects] to this adjunction. Internal abelian groups in presheaves or sheaves of sets are exactly the corresponding abelian presheaves or sheaves: evaluate the addition, zero and inverse maps on each object; their group equations become the sectionwise group axioms, and restriction maps preserve the operations. The lifted left adjoint is therefore abelian sheafification, with underlying set sheafification. By [lem-weil-pbc-large-set-sheafification], its inverted maps are exactly the locally bijective maps, since forgetting abelian structure reflects isomorphisms. Smallness makes the section universe at least as large as both site universes, as all three cited size conventions require. These give precisely the ordinary sheafification hypotheses for step 3.

source.place: Tags 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WM (locally bijective maps); Section 00YR algebraic structures and product-preserving adjunctions

proof.text: Direct sums in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] are coproducts of sheaves. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], two maps $\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal B\to\mathcal H$ agree if they agree on the images of all sectionwise pure tensors. By [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], tensoring with a fixed sheaf preserves coproducts; in the other variable use the sectionwise flip, inverted by flipping again. So each degree of either bracketing of a triple total tensor is the coproduct over $(p,q,r)$ with fixed sum of nested tensors of components, and maps agreeing on every summand agree. On $(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B)\otimes\mathcal G$, two maps to $\mathcal H$ agree if their bilinear maps $\beta,\beta'$ on $(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B)\times\mathcal G$ agree. Let $\mathcal P$ be the presheaf tensor, so $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B=\mathcal P^\#$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $\beta,\beta'$ agree on all $(x\otimes y,z)$, they agree on the image of each $\mathcal P(U)\times\mathcal G(U)$, as $\mathcal P(U)$ is additively generated by pure tensors and $\beta(-,z)$ is additive. By step 1 the underlying set sheaf of $\mathcal P^\#$ is the set sheafification of $\mathcal P$; set sheafification preserves finite products [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] and fixes the sheaf $\mathcal G$, so $\mathcal P^\#\times\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal P\times\mathcal G$ and $\beta=\beta'$. The other bracketing is the same after the flip. Thus maps out of a triple total tensor are determined on nested pure tensors. The index sets are countable subsets of $\mathbf Z^2$, $\mathbf Z^3$ in the allowed universe. No boundedness, and no generation of global sections by global pure sections, is used.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), following bilinear universal-property display; Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints] in the ordinary module-sheaf setting verified in step 1. Its native associator and braiding are natural chain isomorphisms, and its stated pure-section formulas are exactly the unsigned reassociation and the factor $(-1)^{pq}$ required here. By the equality test of step 2, these formulas specify the maps uniquely. For completeness, on a triple of unshifted degrees $(p,q,r)$ the differential on either bracketing has coefficients $1,(-1)^p,(-1)^{p+q}$ on the $dx,dy,dz$ terms after reassociation, so reassociation commutes with the differential. For the flip, $\sigma d$ has coefficients $(-1)^{(p+1)q}$ on $y\otimes dx$ and $(-1)^{p+p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}$ on $dy\otimes x$; $d\sigma$ has coefficients $(-1)^{pq+q}$ and $(-1)^{pq}$ on those same terms. The coefficients agree. Reverse reassociation composes to the identity on each triple summand. Flipping twice gives $(-1)^{pq+qp}=1$ on each bidegree summand. Step 2 therefore identifies the inverses with the two formulas in the statement.

proof.text:
The tensor bifunctor on module sheaves is additive in both variables: the bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] identifies $(f+g)\otimes h$ with $f\otimes h+g\otimes h$, and similarly in the other variable, by evaluation on pure tensors. The category is abelian and has the countable coproducts used in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] to this additive bifunctor, with the first input already shifted by $a$ when applying $s^2_b$. Define
$$t_{a,b}=s^1_a(E,F)[b]\circ s^2_b(E[a],F),$$
followed by the canonical identification $[a][b]=[a+b]$. This is a natural chain isomorphism. The cited node states that $s^2_b$ on first-factor degree $p$ has coefficient $(-1)^{bp}$ and that $s^1_a$ is unsigned. Its composite has exactly the claimed formula, reindexing $(p,q)$ to $(p+a,q+b)$ in $T(E,F)$. Step 2 proves uniqueness from that formula.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor), normalized here using shifted first degree p; Mathlib BifunctorShift.lean lines 95-110, 156-174

proof.text: Check the shift signs directly, so the normalization is independent of any informal identification of shifted and unshifted degrees. Write $x\in E^{p+a}$ and $y\in F^{q+b}$. In $t\,d$ the coefficients of $dx\otimes y$ and $x\otimes dy$ are respectively $(-1)^{a+b(p+1)}$ and $(-1)^{p+b+bp}$. In $d\,t$, using the target shift $[a+b]$, they are $(-1)^{bp+a+b}$ and $(-1)^{bp+a+b+p+a}$. They agree, the second pair differing by $2a$. The reverse reindexing on target degree $(p+a,q+b)$ is assigned the same scalar $(-1)^{bp}$, with $p$ recovered by subtracting $a$; each composite therefore has scalar $(-1)^{2bp}=1$. This proves the inverse formula. In particular the inverse is not being assigned the scalar $(-1)^{b(p+a)}$. The equality test from step 2 gives equality of these chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor); explicit comparison of shifted differentials

proof.text: Naturality can also be checked on the prescribed summands. Chain maps $f:E\to E'$, $g:F\to F'$ and $h:G\to G'$ preserve cochain degree. Either order of applying $t$ and $T(f[a],g[b])$ sends $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{bp}f(x)\otimes g(y)$. Either order for $\sigma$ sends it to $(-1)^{pq}g(y)\otimes f(x)$. Either order for $\alpha$ sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $f(x)\otimes(g(y)\otimes h(z))$. The bilinear universal property and coproduct equality test from step 2 turn these equalities into the naturality squares. The same test proves uniqueness for all the isomorphisms and their inverses.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), naturality part of the constraint verifications

proof.text:
Here is the fully parenthesized first coherence identity, putting $s=a+b+c$ and suppressing only the canonical equalities of shift indices:
$$\alpha_{E,F,G}[s]\circ t_{a+b,c}(T(E,F),G)\circ T(t_{a,b}(E,F),1)
=t_{a,b+c}(E,T(F,G))\circ T(1,t_{b,c}(F,G))\circ\alpha_{E[a],F[b],G[c]}.$$
Both sides start at $T(T(E[a],F[b]),G[c])$ and end at $T(E,T(F,G))[s]$. On a nested pure tensor of shifted degrees $(p,q,r)$, the left route first contributes $bp$ and then $c(p+q)$, since the first input of the outer extraction has shifted degree $p+q$. The final associator is unsigned. The right route first reassociates unsigned, then contributes $cq$, and finally $(b+c)p$. Both have underlying output $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, and
$$bp+c(p+q)=cq+(b+c)p.$$
Their coefficients are therefore equal on every triple summand. The equality test of step 2 proves the chain-map identity. The calculation uses the shifted degrees at the moment of each extraction, not the unshifted degrees $p+a,q+b,r+c$.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes) and More on Algebra item-shift-tensor; explicit triple shift-extraction calculation

proof.text:
For the second coherence identity, take shifted degrees $(p,q)$, so the unshifted degrees of $x,y$ are $p+a,q+b$. On $x\otimes y$, the left composite $\sigma_{E,F}[a+b]\circ t_{a,b}$ has coefficient $(-1)^{bp+(p+a)(q+b)}$ and output $y\otimes x$. The right composite $(-1)^{ab}t_{b,a}\circ\sigma_{E[a],F[b]}$ first flips with coefficient $(-1)^{pq}$ and then extracts shifts from first-factor degree $q$ with coefficient $(-1)^{aq}$, giving $(-1)^{ab+pq+aq}$. The exponents differ by
$$bp+(p+a)(q+b)-(ab+pq+aq)=2bp.$$
Thus the coefficients agree. By step 2 the two maps are equal. This calculation also explains why the outside factor $(-1)^{ab}$ is necessary.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tags 0FNH (item-shift-tensor) and 0GWR (item-flip-tensor-product); shifted-bidegree calculation

proof.text: All sign manipulations above take place in $\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z$: $(-1)^n$ means $1$ for even $n$ and $-1$ for odd $n$, for every integer $n$. Reindexing by an integer is a bijection and preserves the coproduct universal property. Consequently the same constructions and exponent equalities apply to negative shifts and negative cochain degrees. There is no flatness or localization in any step, and neither the double nor triple coproduct argument requires finite support in the degree index of an entire complex. This proves every clause for arbitrary unbounded complexes.
